steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).

Whisk flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and cream of tartar together in a medium bowl. Cut in butter using a pastry cutter or a fork until pea-sized. Make a well in center of the mixture; add milk, Cheddar cheese, and thyme to the well. Gently stir until a soft dough forms.
Roll or pat dough out on a floured surface to ¾-inch thick; cut into circles and place on a baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until biscuit bottoms are golden brown, about 10 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Cheddar-Thyme Flaky Biscuits
raw_recipe.description: These easy-to-make nine-ingredient Cheddar-thyme flaky biscuits rely on a basic biscuit recipe with added shredded Cheddar cheese and chopped fresh thyme.

review.reviewBody: Made these last night with some beef brisket. Cut back on the thyme and found that the sugar made them a little too sweet for my taste. A tip for everyone - put your butter in the freezer for about 15 minutes until really cold and then using the large holes on your grater, grate the butter into the flour mixture. This makes it easier to incorporate the butter and makes a great flaky biscuit. I will definitely make these again but with less sugar.

Delish! Ate 4 of them right out of the oven; so good they didn't even need any butter. Even though I messed up this recipe they came out great. I accidentally added nearly a half cup of flour I had set aside for bench flour to my mixing bowl. I didn't even realize I'd done it until I looked down as I was about to add the milk to the mix and saw my measuring cup of flour was empty. Yikes! I just added extra milk, a little over a cup, total, and just went with that. As others suggested I reduced the sugar to 1 Tbs. and used 1/4 tsp. of dried thyme. It was just the right amount for me. Additions I made were 1/4 tsp. dried parsley, 1/8 tsp. each of onion and garlic powders; all added right into the flour mixture. I also used Lynda's suggestion (the first reviewer) of freezing and grating the butter for easy incorporation into the flour. What a fantastic idea. It made everything go so quick and easy, and way much easier on my arthritic hands. I'm going to use this method for any recipe that requires incorporating butter into flour. Thank you, Lynda, for such a wonderful tip. I've always felt cutting out rounds of biscuits and re-rolling was silly so I just patted the dough into a rectangle and used a pizza cutter to cut 12 square biscuits. Used parchment, and they took 20 minutes to bake--came out light and fluffy and golden. I think next time I'll add a little more cheese and about 2 Tbs. of Parmesan since it gives everything such a nice, nutty taste when it bak

I didn't have the cream of tartar on hand, so I substituted with 1 teaspoon of vinegar. I used frozen butter that had been grated to forgo the cutting in process, and to avoid the messy kneading , I increased the milk so the dough is quite soft, then dropped by teaspoonfuls onto the baking sheet. The less the dough is handled the more flaky the result. Voila! Great flavor and texture. Thanks for the recipe.

I loved this and so did the kids. Easy and fast to make! I sifted all the dry ingredients a couple times and substituted buttermilk. I didn't bother to spread the dough onto a surface, I just let it rest for 10 min then scooped out large spoon sized balls and placed them on baking sheet. I cooked them in countertop toaster oven, and they were awesome.
I added one chopped fresh jalapeño pepper, and used buttermilk instead of regular milk. Also hand formed biscuits rather than rolling them out. Turned out great and received many compliments.

I have made these multiple times with regular flour and just love them. This year company who is Gluten Free and lactose intolerant is coming for Christmas Dinner so I thought I would make a trial run at making these GF, I used King Arthur Flour Measure for Measure (which already has xanthan gum in it) and coconut milk. I grated the butter rather than cutting it in and the dough needed a little extra milk but the end result was really great. They were lovely, light and tasty.

A new favorite in our house. Love it with soups! Altered a bit:
1 tsp dried thyme instead of fresh. Added garlic powder and onion powder to taste. Used only 2 tsp sugar per others' suggestions. I don't have the time to roll out and cut with kids running around so I just used my cookie scoop and dropped rounded balls into a muffin tin! Works just as well and it's way less work in my opinion!
I took 2 of the reviews and reduced sugar to 2 tsp and also froze the butter and grated it in. The biscuits were light and flaky. Went great with fish chowder. Will definitely make again.
Delicious. I added basil and dill and a bit more milk as it seemed too dry to stick together.

I love these! The only modifications I made to this recipe was using dried thyme, as I did not have any fresh on hand, and using a gluten free baking mix (Pamela's) as I do not eat gluten. While the biscuits did not rise as much as they would have done if I had used regular wheat flour the texture was great and the flavor was superb! I also used the tip of grating the butter into the flour mixture and I sifted my dry ingredients to help lighten the dough. Perfection!

I like this recipe. However I prefer my biscuits without the cheese and thyme and half the sugar so I modify the recipe. I also roll and fold the dough several times to get a biscuit with thin delicate layers. Don't add more milk! It will make your biscuits tough. If your biscuits are tough you are likely mixing them too long. You only need to fold the milk in until the dough stays together, overmixing will create gluten strands and make them tough.

Used a good sharp cheddar. Mixed in food processor which was great until I tried scrapping the sticky dough out. Rolled thinner than suggested so didn't get the rise in the recipe photo but delicious just the same.
Added Green onion Superb!
Awesome! I doubled the cheese & added fresh chopped parsley!

No changes made. I followed the recipe to the the "T". They were a big hit and I have made them several times. U se the incredients as was presented though because I tried using dried tyme one time because I didn't have have fresh.. not the same. I make these when I make soups and chili.
Was great but the next time I think I will use more cheese.
I think you could add a bit more milk than what it says

These biscuits were delicious! They were flaky (as the title suggests) and easy to make. I found that they needed a little bit more than ten minutes to cook. That is the only thing that I find wrong with the recipe though. Again - absolutely delicious!
it's a good biscuit, a little sweeet for a savory one, but my family liked them.
i reduced the sugar. really decadent
